outcomes: demonstrate safe working practices in a field construction environment.
demonstrate proper selection, use, care, preparation, and handling of the mill and cabinet carpenter's tools of the trade.
analyze, interpret, and apply national building codes relating to mill and cabinet carpentry.
analyze and interpret residential and commercial construction blueprints.
identify and select appropriate materials for each phase of construction.
construct and complete an advanced project demonstrating journeymen-level skills.
apply design elements and principles to create functional and attractive cabinets.

notes: The text contains no separate Certificate of Achievement section for Mill and Cabinet Maker Apprenticeship; the only section for this program is 'A.A. in Mill and Cabinet Maker Apprenticeship', whose course list matches the closed list exactly. Its requirements (Total Units: 37) were recorded; a reviewer should confirm the certificate's requirements match or locate the certificate section elsewhere in the catalog.

Because the recorded section is the A.A., ge_pattern, degree_total (60, from 'plus sufficient electives for a total of at least 60 units') and electives_fill_degree reflect the degree, not a certificate; drop them if the certificate is recorded separately.
Closed-list code 'CARPT298' (no space) treated as the catalog's 'CARPT 298'.

Several catalog course titles differ from the closed-list titles (e.g., CARPT 270 'Basic Tool Safety for Mill Cabinet', CARPT 271 'Introduction to Mill Cabinet Apprenticeship', CARPT 276 'Hardware Installation', CARPT 278 'Advanced Machinery', CARPT 283 'Introduction to Computer Numeric Control (CNC)'); codes match.
The 16-unit block contains only CARPT 298 (0.5-6 units, repeatable work experience), so 16 units must come from repeated enrollment.
Student learning outcomes are the program's list printed under the A.A. section.
